title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Said to Close Books as IPO Struggles
source_used: Bloomberg text as carried by The Business Times (Singapore), ending with the BLOOMBERG credit. AFR (Street Talk) read only as a paywalled first paragraph for the $8.25 figure. Bloomberg itself blocked (403).
key_facts: Australian data centre company Firmus (Firmus Grid in Bloomberg, Firmus Technologies in AFR) closed its IPO book amid concern that the deal could be pulled, per people familiar.
The close was moved up to Thursday from Friday after early indications from investors well above the offer size; the price and deal structure were not clear at close.
The company sought US$5.5 billion including a greenshoe option, in one of Australia's largest-ever IPOs.
The A$11 marketed price implied a valuation of A$43.7 billion (US$30.4 billion); some investors worried about the pricing and about shareholders flooding the market after listing.
Maas Group, a Firmus backer, fell as much as 30% in Sydney, the most on record.
AFR: bankers worked overnight to save the float at about $8.25 per share after an abrupt reversal in sentiment (AFR figure; currency not stated in the text read).
Proceeds were to fund GPUs for a first data centre project in Batam, Indonesia, with DayOne Data Centers, under an eight-year Nvidia partnership.
quote_evidence: The close of the bookbuilding process was moved up to Thursday from Friday after early indications from investors well in excess of the offer size, people familiar with the matter have said.
The bookbuilding process closed amid reports the company had not attracted adequate support for the A$11 share price marketed to potential investors.

Firmus Technologies has closed off its book-build, with its banking syndicate working overnight to save the float at about $8.25 per share, after an abrupt reversal in the sentiment that was pushing the artificial intelligence infrastructure play towards becoming the biggest float in a generation.
why_it_matters_hint: A test of investor appetite for big AI infrastructure listings; price unclear and the two accounts differ.
event_date: 8 Oct 2026 (book closed on Thursday morning in Australia)
notes: Bloomberg 403 here. Text read in the Business Times copy of the Bloomberg story. Bloomberg's own text says the book closed 'as scheduled' and also that the close was moved up a day; the summary uses 'a day early'. The AFR $8.25 figure is from a paywalled stub; its currency is not stated. Curator follow_up_of 1006:C06-08 (our 6 Oct item on CDC ending its $73.3 billion data centre deal with Firmus).
